Eight THEORYs were filed.

- From Bechtel & Abrahamsen: [THEORY-1290](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1290.md), [THEORY-1289](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1289.md),

- From the critics: [THEORY-1288](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1288.md), [THEORY-1294](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1294.md), [THEORY-1293](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1293.md).

**What the debate does to the record's maintenance claims.** [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)
holds that only interventions on mechanisms, relative to a declared
boundary, separate an internal producer from an outside controller. The
debate sharpens that and does not overturn it.
- **Mutual manipulability does not separate the two.** Both pass its
  conditions. Only its parthood condition does, and that is the boundary
  the experiments presuppose ([CLAIM-530](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-530.md)).
- **Fat-handedness does not reach [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md).** Knocking out a production
  pathway acts only after a delay, so the pathway is a cause even by
  Baumgartner and Gebharter's temporal criterion ([ARG-050](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-050.md), Active).
- **"Realized" has two senses.** Produced through over time is causal and
  shown by intervention. Consists in at a time is underdetermined by
  manipulation data and inferred abductively. The line between them moves
  with the time scale ([CLAIM-528](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-528.md); notes on [CLAIM-515](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-515.md) and [CLAIM-150](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-150.md)).
- **The constructions are de novo, how-possibly models.** In Bechtel and
  Abrahamsen's sense, [CASE-189](../../record/cases.d/CASE-189.md) and [CASE-190](../../record/cases.d/CASE-190.md) can show how a maintained
  organization could behave, not that any real one does. Their knockouts
  are clamping tests (notes on both cases).
- **Griesemer and Shavit's modes of interaction.** Only those criteria
  stated on interactions can individuate an organization without
  presupposing it ([CLAIM-529](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-529.md)). Generative entrenchment alone does
  not give closure ([CLAIM-531](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-531.md)).

**For the owner.**
- Three free copies await only a browser:
  - Craver, Glennan & Povich 2021, which would settle whether "causal
    betweenness" lets the outside controller in;
  - Krickel 2018;
  - Romero 2015 and Harinen 2018, on PhilSci-Archive.
- A TLS note. To fetch Bechtel's UCSD copies, one reader added Mozilla's
  standard CA bundle, because the configured bundle lacked that site's
  root certificate. Verification stayed on.

Six THEORYs were filed.
- **Mental autonomy:** [THEORY-1297](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1297.md), [THEORY-1300](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1300.md), [THEORY-1298](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1298.md)
  and [THEORY-1296](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1296.md), all Proposed.
- **Experience:** [THEORY-1299](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1299.md) (Proposed) and [THEORY-1295](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1295.md)
  (Active).

**What the readings do to the record.**
- **Will-organization.** Mind-wandering, on Metzinger's account, is a
  recurring loss of the ability to suspend one's own mental processes. The
  ability is kept and its representation lost, which in structure is
  will-organization. It does not yet support [CLAIM-027](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-027.md) ([ARG-051](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-051.md),
  Proposed):
  - he attributes each episode's onset to cued goal states;
  - his 2017 chapter leaves open whether the self-model's representation
    causes, enables or only accompanies control ([QUESTION-367](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-367.md)).
- **His figure.** His "roughly two thirds" of waking life does not follow
  from his own figures, which give 52%.
- **Evidence for experience.** The minimal case is a "nonegoic"
  self-model with no world and no felt oneness, which narrows [THEORY-063](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-063.md).
  - The book calls selfless consciousness empirically established, while
    its methods chapter calls remembered reports of selfless states
    "highly dubious" evidence ([THEORY-1295](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1295.md)).
  - [QUESTION-368](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-368.md) asks whether experience without self-model or
    valence would ground moral standing.
- **Dated notes.**
  - Will line: [TERM-023](../../record/terms.d/TERM-023.md) and nine claims and questions.
  - Experience line: [QUESTION-255](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-255.md), [CLAIM-412](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md), [CLAIM-355](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-355.md), [QUESTION-046](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-046.md),
    [QUESTION-048](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-048.md), [QUESTION-254](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-254.md), [TERM-045](../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md), [TERM-082](../../record/terms.d/TERM-082.md) and [TERM-083](../../record/terms.d/TERM-083.md).
  - Readings: [THEORY-063](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-063.md), [THEORY-064](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-064.md) and [NOTE-1058](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1058.md). The two THEORYs now
    record *Being No One* as Unavailable, not Deferred.

**Inconsistencies in the book.** It gives 841 usable reports with more
than 500 printed (p. xvi), and also "1,183 written ... reports presented
in this book" (p. 17).

**For the owner.** "Artificial suffering" needs only a browser:
philarchive.org/archive/METASA-4. The readers suggest two works for later
reading: Pezzulo's 2018 commentary on the 2017 chapter, and Axelrod et
al. 2015, the first test of Metzinger's H1.

## Yang and Abanin, integrals of motion as slow modes: read in full and filed for the scale-separation line, with two THEORYs and notes on three claims

*2026-11-02 01:51:50*

The owner asked whether arXiv:2506.02970 bears on the record, then asked for
it to be read and filed. Before filing, a search of the record for
Lindbladian, integrals of motion, slow modes, operator growth and
open-system terms found no earlier work in open quantum many-body dynamics.
The paper bears on the scale-separation line and the slowness readings next
to it, not on the quantum-foundations material.

| work | code | status | copy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yang and Abanin, "Integrals of motion as slow modes in dissipative many-body operator dynamics" (2025) | [LIT-1958](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1958.md) | Active, [NOTE-1534](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1534.md) Read | arXiv v3 with its supplementary material |

The citation was checked against arXiv metadata and Crossref, sending no
email address ([ADR-008](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-008.md)). The text was extracted with pypdf (PyMuPDF and
pdftotext are not on this host), and the figures came through as captions
only.

**Filed from it.**
- [THEORY-1323](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1323.md) (Active): what the paper derived exactly and what exact
  diagonalization showed at nine sites or fewer, with the ranking's
  dependence on noise strength.
- [THEORY-1343](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1343.md) (Proposed): the large-system argument through a gap of
  order min(γL, √(v_Bγ)), which the authors qualify themselves.

**What the reading does to the record.** Dated notes, none changing a claim:
- **[CLAIM-478](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md).** A route to separation, conservation under weak local
  noise with operator growth setting the fast rate, and support for the
  first half.
- **[CLAIM-331](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md).** What slowness marks depends on the environment, on a
  measure of size, and on the noise strength.
- **[CLAIM-394](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-394.md).** A non-self-adjoint generator where slow-decaying and
  eigen-directions nearly coincide under a small parameter.

**Not flagged `anthology-candidate`.** The paper carries no instruction for
machine-learning practice, and the anthology's topics are about ML. Its
cited neighbours (Mori 2024; Jacoby, Huse and Gopalakrishnan 2025; Wurtz
and Polkovnikov; Moudgalya and Motrunich 2024) are not held here. They
would be the next reading if the line wants the Mori gap itself.

owner then supplied the manuscript under its PhilArchive record ID,

fetched, read in full in [NOTE-1508](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1508.md). Of its main sources, two

Each Unfetched status note gives the address that failed, so the generated
status page is the owner's queue ([ADR-053](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-053.md)). Each Unavailable note says where
the reader looked.

**Status of the THEORYs** follows the readers' checks. A THEORY is Active
where the paper establishes it and the reader checked it, by re-derivation,
recomputation from the paper's tables, or an independent simulation (Slemp et
al.'s Table 2 from Table 1; Donoghue et al.'s waveform artefact; the
Sánchez-Cañizares model; LDA's agreement formula). It is Proposed where the
evidence is correlational in a way the theory's causal reading needs, or
argument without a model.

**What the readings corrected.**

- **In the registrations of 2026-11-02.**
  - Ryan et al. 2022 is not "the nearest thing to an audit": it is a narrative
    map by the theory's co-founder, not preregistered, grading no
    meta-analysis.
  - Ntoumanis et al. do not supply the intervention evidence [THEORY-052](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-052.md) asks
    for: they measure no need frustration and test no mediation.
  - Murphy et al.'s objection is to the satisfaction–frustration *split* and
    to items with no thwarting content, broader than "the frustration factor".
  - Persona Vectors fits no persona distribution.
  - Slemp et al.'s evidence is associational; its authors take direction "on
    theoretical grounds".
  - Patrick et al. 2007 does not use the name "relationships motivation
    theory"; it is a study the mini-theory was built on.
  - Voigt 2022 is an Opinion article, not a review.
  - Ben-Tal et al.'s in-between case restricts the rule's form, not what it
    reads; and their online date, 2003-08-08, is now `published:`.
  The LITs' histories record each.
- **In the exchange's replies and in this branch's entries.**
  - Jennings's uses of her sources: Szczepanski et al. are correlational, so
    "improve" is not supported; Voigt proposes the value update and its
    attention is bottom-up, against [THEORY-1341](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1341.md)'s dlPFC criterion;
    Anastassiou et al. explain field effects by circuit physics, against her
    inference from them; and the constraint without downward causation is
    Bishop's own (2024 SEP), so what is hers is the boundary condition and the
    causal-power step. [NOTE-1508](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1508.md) and [THEORY-1314](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1314.md) are corrected.
  - [CLAIM-536](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-536.md): smoothed LDA's topic priors are draws from one shared
    Dirichlet, and the Assistant Axis's input-driven switching fits neither
    limit. [TERM-064](../../record/terms.d/TERM-064.md)'s note: "QK/OV circuit" is Elhage et al.'s vocabulary.
  - [CLAIM-533](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md): Froese, a libertarian, concedes its core; the irruption
    model has no chaos. Kane himself is still unread.
- **In the record.**
  - [THEORY-049](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-049.md) said Ryan et al. 1983 found its pattern "not significantly"; the
    primary paper reports a significant contrast.
  - [THEORY-052](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-052.md): Campbell et al. give no temporal order; Levine et al. are the
    first prospective evidence; the frustration scale's split is organized by
    keying.
  - [NOTE-439](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-439.md)'s C4, [NOTE-441](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-441.md)'s C8 and [NOTE-442](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-442.md) are qualified against their
    primary sources; [NOTE-440](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-440.md)'s "derivative" reply answers SDT's own
    researchers.
  - [LIT-1132](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1132.md)'s note of 2026-11-02 overstated what the 2026 paper covers, and its
    body still called [LIT-588](../../record/literature.d/LIT-588.md) Unavailable.

**Errors found in the papers** are in the NOTEs: Murphy et al.'s Discussion

| 8 | Nested cooperation, local against collective interest at each scale | the distributed-agency line, [QUESTION-083](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-083.md) above all |

## What was missing, and is now filed

- **Four works, registered Deferred and unread:**
  - West et al. 2015, [LIT-2003](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2003.md);
  - Henrich and Muthukrishna 2021, [LIT-2004](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2004.md);
  - Van Lange and Bergmann 2026, [LIT-2002](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2002.md);
  - Maynard Smith and Szathmáry, *The Major Transitions in Evolution*, [LIT-2001](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2001.md).

  The synthesis names the first and last as foundational and cites the
  middle two in §4 and §7. Each entry says where a copy is listed, and
  none has been fetched.
- **[CLAIM-546](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-546.md)** (§3, demonstrated). Coexistence by frequency
  dependence is not cooperation: Hawk–Dove coexists at V/C Hawks with
  exploitation intact. The record held the Black Queen case and the
  invasion criterion, not the point.
- **[CLAIM-547](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-547.md)** (§7, interpretive). Cooperation within groups and
  the coexistence of groups can trade off, and Nowak's group-selection
  rule is an exact instance. Its cooperation is bought by group
  extinction, which the reader checked against the paper's text. Local
  cooperation, coexistence of groups and impartial concern are three
  achievements.
- **[QUESTION-371](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-371.md)** (§9). Can moral norms be stabilizing mechanisms
  among groups in Chesson's sense?

## Left as it is

- **§2's cited work on facilitation and mutualism stabilizing
  coexistence.** The synthesis cites only an ESA journal on Wiley,
  without a title. A search turned up candidates but not that work, so
  nothing is registered. The record holds no work on positive
  interactions in coexistence theory, and [CLAIM-546](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-546.md) says so.
- **§2's Nature citation on mitochondria.** It names no paper. The record
  holds the Nature papers on the subject: [LIT-1591](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1591.md), [LIT-1595](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1595.md), [LIT-1558](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1558.md).
- **The research-programme question of §8**, on stable mutual benefit
  without loss of diversity or autonomy. It is the distributed-agency
  line's own question, and [QUESTION-083](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-083.md) and [QUESTION-132](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-132.md) hold its parts.
- **§9's other questions.** The question on institutions giving the
  benefits of interdependence without loss of autonomy is [QUESTION-083](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-083.md)'s
  for groups. The question on widening the circle needs no new entry.
  The question on moral disagreement as conflict between cooperative
  problems is morality-as-cooperation's own programme ([THEORY-468](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-468.md), [NOTE-408](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-408.md)).
- **The direct-reciprocity widget** (b = 5, c = 2, w = 60% against a
  threshold of 40%). It is [THEORY-567](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-567.md)'s w > c/b with numbers.
- **The closing line**, "evolution … selects among ways of organizing
  relationships". It is a slogan and is not filed.

## Readings, added 2026-11-04

At the owner's "read them", three readers fetched lawful copies. Every
quote the filing leans on was rechecked against the text.

- **West et al. 2015** ([LIT-2003](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2003.md)), read in full from PubMed Central:
  [NOTE-1538](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1538.md), [THEORY-1351](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1351.md). §2's list is right about the abstract and
  loose about the body. Only mutual dependence and negligible (not
  "reduced") conflict are defining conditions, and the two occur apart.
  Notes were added to [CLAIM-474](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md), [QUESTION-277](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-277.md) and [THEORY-141](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md).
- **Van Lange and Bergmann 2026** ([LIT-2002](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2002.md)), read in full from the
  first author's own posting: [NOTE-1537](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1537.md), [THEORY-1352](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1352.md). §7 is right,
  with a refinement: lower cooperation between groups needs only
  categorization, and harm needs conflicting interests. The entry's second
  author is corrected to Paul K. Bergmann, and the article is a
  Perspective. Notes were added to [CLAIM-547](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-547.md), which the reading
  supports on one link, and to [QUESTION-371](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-371.md), which it does not answer.
- **Henrich and Muthukrishna 2021** ([LIT-2004](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2004.md)) was not reached. The
  authors' lab PDF answers this client with HTTP 403, and no other open
  copy exists. Now Unfetched. §4's characterization is unverified.
- **Maynard Smith and Szathmáry** ([LIT-2001](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2001.md)) has no lawful open copy.
  Now Unavailable.

## Support, added 2026-11-04

Under [ADR-061](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-061.md), an ARG is filed where the record says something about
support. One filing did. Van Lange and Bergmann were cited as the human
case of [CLAIM-547](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-547.md) before they were read, and the reading carries only
the claim's first link. That verdict is [ARG-052](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-052.md) (source, Rejected as
an inference to the claim as titled). The review moves from the claim's
grounds to corroboration: [THEORY-1352](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1352.md) corroborates [CLAIM-547](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-547.md)
([ADR-058](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-058.md)). West et al.'s Table 1 is independent evidence for [CLAIM-474](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md), so
[THEORY-1351](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1351.md) corroborates it; no doubt about that support is in
question, so it needs no ARG. West et al. and [THEORY-141](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md) differ on which
mechanism mattered most, not on what is possible, so they are not rivals,
and the note on [THEORY-141](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md) is enough.

  splits into structural and governance cases. See [CLAIM-554](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-554.md) and the
  note on [QUESTION-131](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-131.md).

  - a changed H¹ class;
  - cutting the witnessing cycle;

  "already supplies" a definition of psychological flexibility; it doesn't.

## What A got wrong, across the works

- **Quotations.** None of the sentences A put in quotation marks occurs in
  any of the twelve papers. Each NOTE records A's as paraphrase.
- **Rival models.** The models A says were outperformed are often weak:
  - Kemp et al. (2010) compared only two simple baselines, by curve shape.
  - Lucas and Griffiths's rivals cannot vary across conditions.
  - In Baker et al., a cue-based heuristic matched the Bayesian model on
    Experiment 1's belief judgements.
  - In Jiang and Lucas, the ablation without transfer won the group-level
    comparison; the transfer account rests on the per-participant count.
- **"Hierarchical".** The word is A's label for Körding et al. and Baker
  et al., not the papers'. A places the hierarchical Gaussian filter
  beside HDDM, as estimation across participants. Its levels are hidden
  states inside one learner, and its parameters are fitted per subject.
  A's own table row, "Hierarchical Bayesian filtering", is the right place.
- **Mechanisms.** Gershman, Blei and Niv's model is a static mixture with
  no "transition". Context there is observed; the latent cause is what is
  inferred.
- **Experiments counted.**
  - Kemp et al. (2007) runs no experiments.
  - Körding et al.'s second "experiment" re-models Wallace et al. (2004).
  - Collins et al. (2014) re-analyses the participants of Collins and
    Frank's Experiment 2.
  - Mathys et al. (2011) fits no human data, and the 2014 paper fits one
    subject.
- **Lake et al.** The caveat that people may not use the same programs is
  A's. The authors suggest people do infer abstract motor programs.
- **Attribution.**
  - A's "Lucas and colleagues" is Lucas and Griffiths.
  - The registries give Kemp et al. 2007's second author as "Andrew
    Perfors"; the byline reads Amy Perfors.
  - The registries list only Mathys for the 2011 paper, which has four
    authors.

## What was left, and why

- **A's framing (§1).** The φ → θᵢ → Dᵢ schema, and the claim that hierarchy
  explains learning from little data and transfer, are the textbook
  framing. They are A's summary, not a finding, and the THEORYs hold what
  each paper shows.
- **A's criteria (§4).** Transfer, non-obvious predictions, comparison
  against simpler alternatives on held-out data, and recovery of
  meaningful latent variables. They are reasonable, but A applied them to
  the papers loosely, as above. They are not filed as a claim: this is the
  first time they turn up.
- **The four-way table and closing distinction (§§3, 5).** Abstract
  knowledge, latent structure, parameter estimation and filtering is a
  usable taxonomy, and the readings support it once the HGF is placed
  correctly. It is left in this entry rather than given a code, until it
  recurs.
- **A's reading list (§5).** It is advice and is not filed.

## What A got wrong, across the works

- **Quotations.** A's quoted sentences for Oskar, Ratliff, Liebman,
  Siemroth and Bogetoft are in none of the texts. They are A's paraphrases.
- **The USFA case.**
  - The page cancels one tanker and one rescue vehicle over a false alarm,
    not "rescue and support vehicles".
  - There is no heavy rescue squad on it.
  - Calls a department could not answer for lack of resources fall outside
    NFIRS altogether, and a separate record of them is recommended, not
    required. That gap is the readiness case A wanted, and A missed it.
- **Overstatements.**
  - McLay & Mayorga's headline is that 7- and 8-minute standards also
    maximize survival.
  - Siemroth finds full rollover optimal for most parameter values.
  - Halfin & Whitt's capacity is busy, not idle reserve.
  - Jordan & Graves is a simulation study, not "a mathematical study".
  - ReVelle & Hogan's comparison is with other coverage models, not with
    "utilization maximization".
  - Larson's model computes workloads, not "a unit's value".
- **Missed mechanisms.** Liebman & Mahoney's precautionary buffer, and the
  hypercube model's units of last resort, are the papers' own ties to
  readiness.

## What A got wrong, across the works

- **Quotations.** A's quoted lines for Berry et al. and Murray and
  Sastry, and its sentences for Zang et al., Chen, Choi and Mahadevan, Li
  and Choi and Stern, Pinson and Murugan, are A's paraphrases.
- **Attribution.**
  - the point that redundant constraints create states of self-stress is
    Damavandi et al.'s, not Rocks and Mehta's;
  - the origami-springs paper's title was wrong;
  - "morphological computation" is A's label for Dollar and Howe.
- **Overstatements.**
  - FACT's 26 matching pairs hold only for ideal pure-force constraints;
  - the 64 switch states are a counting convention, the defects were
    reached by hand, and height and stiffness do not identify every
    state;
  - DeLuca et al.'s trapping is simulated, found in the large design, and
    not called nucleation;
  - the origami reservoir learns only in its linear readout;
  - Zang et al.'s frustration is prestress applied from outside;
  - the interface freedoms of Kane and Lubensky and of Chen et al. need
    unequal polarizations, and otherwise give stressed lines;
  - A's bottleneck budget keeps only the lowest barrier (Mirth et al.).
- **Missed.** Stern, Pinson and Murugan's main point: actuator placement
  predicts success far better than count.

## What A got wrong

- **The CSP dichotomy.** It classifies decision problems over fixed finite
  languages, not "computational systems", and says nothing about how
  solutions connect. The polymorphism algebra A calls "the algebraic
  component" does not decide navigation: in Gopalan et al.'s phrase, the
  boundaries "cut across Boolean clones". The lead checked by enumeration
  that two languages with the same trivial clone fall on opposite sides.
- **Eppstein.** NP-completeness of flat folding is earlier work. A missed
  the paper's Galois-theory result (folded shapes not expressible in
  radicals), which qualifies A's dismissal of Galois groups.
- **Resource composition.** A's cost laws do not come from Coecke, Fritz
  and Spekkens, whose conversions are free. A's "resource-graded" category
  is the standard graded (locally graded) category. Multiparameter
  persistence is of wild type, a stronger limit than A states.
- **Akitaya et al.** "Infinitesimal" should be small finite motions from
  flat, and the result holds for general crease patterns.
- **The askable set.** A presented it as new; [CLAIM-475](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-475.md) holds it.

## The assistant's contributions

- **[CLAIM-594](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-594.md),** demonstrated. When the resource that pays for crossing
  barriers also sets the costs it pays, as heat does, reaching a target
  within a time budget is a window in the resource, more time widens it,
  and a schedule can reach what no constant level reaches. The record's
  fixed-cost budgeted reachability is the special case. It is corroborated
  by the dissertation's narrow folding window and hysteresis, by
  Wagenbauer et al.'s stepped schedule and by Dannenberg et al.'s
  rate-dependent hysteresis ([THEORY-1440](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1440.md), [THEORY-1443](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1443.md),
  [THEORY-1447](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1447.md)).
- **[CASE-216](../../record/cases.d/CASE-216.md),** its construction: a four-state annealing toy with
  free energies linear in temperature, computed with python3 -I. Within
  one hour the best constant temperature reaches 90.4 % folded and none
  reaches 95 %. Five minutes at 327 K then 318 K reaches 98.5 %.
- **Notes read across the readings,** on [QUESTION-374](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-374.md), [CLAIM-570](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-570.md),

  - observers coarser than the system are the common case (Dunn et al.'s
    routings, DeLuca et al.'s hybridization states);
  - staple excess is standing slack against spend-matching;
  - a second account of traps (Sobczak's dissertation) beside DeLuca et

  also changed its scaffold route. "Optimizing a developmental mechanism"
  goes beyond an equilibrium model.
- **Majikes et al. 2026** is in Nucleic Acids Research, not an RSC journal.

**[CLAIM-599](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-599.md),** demonstrated. Establishing more relations can lower the

upward. Two productive nuclei can combine into a trap: V(∅) = 0.2,

[CLAIM-347](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)'s jointly satisfiable sets, which are closed downward, the
productive sets have no closure. Dunn et al.'s seams and Majikes et al.
2026's short folds are the molecular instances.

- **A correction to this filing.** [QUESTION-399](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-399.md) said that nothing in the
  origami read here repairs itself, and [QUESTION-090](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-090.md)'s note said no reading
  reached replacement of damaged parts. Scheckenbach et al. show both are
  wrong. Folded origami replaces labels and missing staples from a strand
  pool, and in serum keeps 76 % intact over 11 days against 12 %. Both
  entries are corrected in place, saying what they said before.
- **Correction is internal, its supply external.** Proofreading tiles turn a
  mismatch into a stall, so the error falls off before it is locked in. At
  a target error rate of 10⁻⁴ this buys about 10⁴ in speed, and it fails on
  facet errors, which, in the authors' words, need "Some other error-correcting strategy". The value
  of correction depends on which errors dominate ([CLAIM-520](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-520.md)).
- **Barriers can be designed in or out.** Cumberworth et al. find no barrier
  in typical designs, and one of about 10 kBT at the melting temperature
  where stacking between staples is strong. It vanishes a few degrees
  lower. This is consistent with their 2025 review.

- **The supply is not neutral.** [CLAIM-597](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md)'s supplied repair leaves the

  lowers it, by the Samaritan's dilemma, by unused revenue machinery
  decaying, or by funding for form crowding out function.

  and motivation together, linkages formed early, and gradual exit in which
  participants operated independently before closure. Azam et al.'s
  optimal exit instead cuts aid up front, and their recipient is better off

## The assistant's contributions

- **[CLAIM-604](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md)** (demonstrated) connects [CLAIM-597](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md) to the dissipative
  structures. Upkeep that a structure draws in through its own intact
  state, as a flame does, has an ignition threshold, a supply level below
  which it collapses, and an outage after which it does not relight.
  Supplied upkeep has none of the three. It gives [QUESTION-085](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-085.md) three
  signatures to look for in placement records.
- **[CLAIM-602](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md)** (demonstrated) models aid crowding out capacity that is
  learned by doing.
  - Azam et al. already have kept capacity falling with aid's share, and
    the claim credits them.
  - Not in their paper: recovery after exit grows linearly with how long aid
    did all the work, because work is capped by capacity. Aid used after
    the organization's own capacity leaves its learning untouched.
  - Azam et al. call the harmful rule "gap-filling", so the benign one is
    named capacity-first.
- **[CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md)** (interpretive), after the owner remarked that assured
  help making recipients lose skill "sounds closely related to niche
  differentiation and specialization phenomena". The loss is the Black
  Queen's ([THEORY-1048](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md)), favoured to the one who loses it. Whether it is
  dependency or division of labour is set by the supply: one-way supply
  from outside limits nothing and punishes withdrawal, while reciprocal
  loss, as in Buchnera ([THEORY-1103](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md)), gives interdependence. So
  self-sufficiency may be better framed as reciprocity. A dated note goes
  on [QUESTION-277](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-277.md).
- **Reproduction.** scratch/formal/supplied_maintenance_toys.py asserts
  every number in both claims.

**[CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md)** (interpretive) is the assistant's answer. Transient
support can be withdrawn safely when three conditions hold:
- it starts a self-sustaining process on a flux that stays available;
- the threat it stood in for has gone;
- the supported party did the work throughout.

Support that does the work wears capacity down by disuse, by slack effort
and, fastest, by selection for the supported conditions. Which kind of
support it was shows only in persistence through a full turnover after
withdrawal. The claim also records what the readings do not support:
- thresholds and hysteresis are rare in the field;
- longer support is not always worse;
- the evidence is not strong.

  - Balboni, Bandiera, Burgess, Ghatak and Heil ([LIT-2149](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2149.md)), read
    from NBER.
  - Haushofer and Fehr 2014 ([LIT-2152](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2152.md)).
- **Urban.**
  - Kline and Moretti 2014 on the Tennessee Valley Authority
    ([LIT-2141](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2141.md)).
  - Michaels et al. 2021 on sites-and-services ([LIT-2168](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2168.md)), read from
    the accepted manuscript.
  - Neumark and Simpson on place-based policy ([LIT-2158](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2158.md)), read from
    an NBER draft.
  - Collins and Shester 2013 ([LIT-2161](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2161.md)) and LaVoice 2024
    ([LIT-2142](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2142.md)) on urban renewal.
  - Ostrom 1996 on coproduction is Unavailable ([LIT-2140](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2140.md)). It was
    read through Evans 1996 ([LIT-2143](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2143.md)) and Watson 1995
    ([LIT-2190](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2190.md)).
- **Not reached.** Jane Jacobs's argument on gradual and cataclysmic
  money: no lawful copy, and nothing is written about it.
- **Dates.** The lead set Collins and Shester's date at first to a
  Crossref deposit date. The filer flagged it, and it is now the month's
  first day under [ADR-002](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-002.md).
- **Interruption.** The container restarted during the coproduction
  filing. The filer resumed from its transcript, and its partial files
  survived.

**What changed.** The household evidence contradicts slack effort as a
general route: cash barely changes work, and graduation packages raise
it. [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) is revised.
- Its title adds a condition on size, after Balboni et al.'s asset
  threshold. Support too small decays without dependence.
- The supported party must be able to do the work, after Michaels et al.
- Inputs the party cannot produce are a standing part of the
  arrangement, after Evans and Watson.
- Persistence after withdrawal is necessary but not sufficient, since
  slow reversion can mimic it, after Kline and Moretti.
- The unit whose persistence counts must be the one the support was for,
  after Collins and Shester and LaVoice.

[CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md), [CLAIM-602](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) and [CLAIM-604](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md) gain sections on the
new readings. Dated notes go on [QUESTION-398](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-398.md) and [CLAIM-597](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md).

## Deprivation as time pressure, windfalls and scarcity

The owner read Haushofer and Fehr's finding as decision-making under a
resource constraint: "deprivation induces added time pressure to the
decision making process". They also suggested lottery winners as cases of
large, sudden money.

- **The assistant's claim.** [CLAIM-601](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-601.md) (demonstrated) holds that a
  savings buffer is a stock of time, with scratch/formal/deprivation_horizon_toy.py.
- **Windfalls read.**
  - Cesarini et al. ([LIT-2166](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2166.md)), from the working paper.
  - Golosov et al. ([LIT-2181](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2181.md)), from NBER.
  - Hankins, Hoekstra and Skiba ([LIT-2184](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2184.md)), from a 2009 draft. The
    lead's brief named a wrong NBER number for it, and the LIT records the
    error.
- **Scarcity read.**
  - Shah, Mullainathan and Shafir 2012 is Unavailable ([LIT-2147](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2147.md)). It
    was read through its working paper ([LIT-2171](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2171.md)) and the authors'
    replications ([LIT-2157](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2157.md)).
  - Camerer et al. 2018 ([LIT-2162](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2162.md)).
  - The working paper and the replications write-up carry no date. They
    are dated from their PDFs' creation stamps at month precision, an
    exception to this filing's practice made because nothing else dates
    them.

**What changed.**
- The windfall readings confirm that slack effort lives where help is
  large, unconditional and permanent, modestly and without a threshold.
  They show that a lump sum postpones rather than prevents distress when
  it starts nothing that keeps going. [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) gains a section on
  windfalls.
- The scarcity readings correct the owner's framing and the assistant's
  claim. The authors themselves tested time pressure as a confound and
  found scarcity of a clockless resource changed choices too, so time
  pressure is one instance, not the route. [CLAIM-601](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-601.md) gains a section
  saying so.

## Corrections during the filing

- A phrase that Moss et al. use to paraphrase Azam et al. had been
  attributed to Azam et al. in the Moss NOTE and in [CLAIM-602](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md). Both
  now name it as Moss et al.'s paraphrase.
- A sentence comparing recovery under Azam et al.'s law was dropped from
  [CLAIM-602](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md), because it came from the reader's own derivation and was
  not checked.

## What was left, and why

- **Kaldor 1963**, Moore's IDS Working Paper 280, Ross 2004 and Knack 2001
  are cited by the readings and not registered.
- **A threshold version of the crowding-out model**, in which capacity
  regrows only from above a level, as Azam et al.'s trap suggests: stated
  as a limit of [CLAIM-602](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md), not modelled.

## Gap-filling, the models: the capability trap and tapering, after the supplied-maintenance filing

*2026-11-05 23:38:29*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: CLAIM-602 CLAIM-604 CLAIM-605 — Proposed or new; claims this filing writes or extends -->

The owner asked the assistant to "merge 404 then proceed systematically
filling all of those identified gaps". The gaps were the ones the
assistant listed after the supplied-maintenance filing. This branch takes
the models among them. The readings go on branches of their own
([ADR-071](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-071.md)).

- **Built.** [CLAIM-605](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md), with scratch/formal/capability_trap_toy.py.
  - Threshold learning gives full substitution a deadline, 3.10 time
    units in the example.
  - A taper of substitutive support longer than 9.13 periods traps a
    party that an abrupt cut would have saved.
  - Capacity-first support needs no taper and cannot ignite.

  The assistant had guessed 6.8 periods for the longest safe taper.
  Bisection gave 9.13, and the script asserts the bisected value.
- **Reconciled.** Azam et al.'s optimal up-front cut, for substitutive
  aid, and the Kenya exit study's success with gradual exits, in which
  participants already did the work.
- **Not built, and why.**
  - Coproduction with a standing input. Output that needs both parties'
    inputs collapses when either is withdrawn by definition. A model
    would restate what [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) already holds from Evans and Watson.
  - Attention as a capacity, distinct from the buffer as a reserve.
    Modelling it needs a decision process the record has not read, and
    is left open.
- **A dated note** goes on [CLAIM-602](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md), whose limit this models.

The owner asked the assistant to "proceed systematically filling all of

aid-dependency claims rested on review essays. This branch sought
identified state-level evidence.

  ([LIT-2219](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2219.md)), from World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 2396.

## Gap-filling, medicine: supply that suppresses a gland, support that atrophies a muscle, and how patients are weaned

*2026-11-05 23:52:49*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: CLAIM-558 CLAIM-597 CLAIM-600 CLAIM-602 LIT-2212 LIT-2213 — Proposed or Unavailable; entries this filing notes or registers -->

The owner asked the assistant to "proceed systematically filling all of
those identified gaps". This branch takes medicine, the most quantitative
case of supply suppressing a system's own production and of tapering.

- **Corticosteroids.**
  - Broersen et al. 2015 ([LIT-2214](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2214.md)), read from the reprint in
    Broersen's open Leiden thesis.
  - The 2024 ESE/Endocrine Society guideline ([LIT-2218](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2218.md)).
- **Ventilation.**
  - Levine et al. 2008 ([LIT-2212](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2212.md)) is Unavailable. It was read through
    Jaber et al. 2011 ([LIT-2211](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2211.md)) and Goligher et al. 2020
    ([LIT-2216](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2216.md)).
  - Boles et al. 2007 ([LIT-2213](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2213.md)) is Unavailable. It was read through
    Shah, Hart and Kaltsakas 2024 ([LIT-2217](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2217.md)) and Alía and Esteban 2000
    ([LIT-2215](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2215.md)).
- **Attributions corrected by the lead.** The lead's first drafts of the
  notes credited three weaning figures to the wrong neighbour. The figures
  are 75 % abrupt withdrawal, about 13 % reintubation, and the equivalence
  of 30- and 120-minute trials. They are Alía and Esteban's, and the notes
  now say so.
- **What changed.**
  - Supply that does a gland's work suppresses it, more with dose and
    duration. The guideline's cure is to cover the shortfall: capacity
    first.
  - Full ventilatory support atrophies the diaphragm within days, and
    effort has a band, not just a floor.
  - For most patients, abrupt removal after a passed readiness trial is
    the course. The method that tapers machine breaths did worst.
  - No corticosteroid taper scheme is shown to be safe or efficient.
  - These agree with the assistant's capability-trap claim, filed
    separately in dmarx/nucleation#405, on abrupt cuts of substitutive
    support.

  Dated notes go on [CLAIM-558](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md), [CLAIM-597](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md), [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md), [CLAIM-602](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) and
  [QUESTION-398](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-398.md).

<!-- inactive-ok-file: CLAIM-600 CLAIM-604 CLAIM-606 LIT-2210 LIT-2199 LIT-2194 LIT-2195 LIT-2209 — Proposed, Unavailable, Unfetched or new; entries this filing writes, notes or registers -->

The owner wrote: "I have a hunch the physics/dynamics of soliton formation
could be a valuable angle through which to consider some of our questions
about individuation and persistence". The assistant proposed, from memory,
three routes to persistence, and had them checked against readings.

- **Read.**
  - Herr et al. 2014 ([LIT-2204](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2204.md)), from arXiv v3.
  - Grelu and Akhmediev 2012 ([LIT-2196](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2196.md)), from the authors' HAL
    manuscript.
  - Grimshaw, Smyth and Stepanyants 2018 ([LIT-2198](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2198.md)).
  - Zabusky and Porter's Scholarpedia entry ([LIT-2208](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2208.md)).
  - Cui and Wang ([LIT-2202](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2202.md)) and Zheng et al. ([LIT-2203](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2203.md)).
  - Copeland, Gleiser and Müller 1995 ([LIT-2200](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2200.md)).
  - Fodor 2019 ([LIT-2197](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2197.md), Skimmed) and Tong's lectures ([LIT-2207](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2207.md),
    Skimmed).
- **Not read.**
  - Kivshar and Malomed 1989 ([LIT-2210](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2210.md)): closed.
  - Zabusky and Kruskal 1965 ([LIT-2199](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2199.md)) and Satsuma and Yajima 1974
    ([LIT-2194](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2194.md)): free copies located but blocked by Cloudflare.
  - Purwins et al. 2010 ([LIT-2195](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2195.md)) and Akhmediev and Ankiewicz 2008
    ([LIT-2209](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2209.md)): closed.
- **Corrections to the assistant's sketch.**
  - Identity through collisions belongs to integrable systems, not to
    conservative ones in general.
  - Herr et al. never name hysteresis; they show path dependence.
  - The formation threshold for an integrable soliton is a reader's
    derivation from a quoted formula, not a sentence in any source.
- **The assistant's claim.** [CLAIM-606](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md) sets out three routes: internal
  balance, supplied balance and topological charge, with the oscillon as a
  fourth case. Its main consequence is a qualification of [CLAIM-604](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md):
  thresholds and abrupt ends appear without self-sustaining upkeep, so
  only withdrawing the supply identifies the route.
- **Dated notes** go on [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md), [CLAIM-604](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md), [QUESTION-085](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-085.md) and

## Works filed Unavailable that ADR-053 files as Unfetched, swept; Suding et al. 2004 read from a copy ADR-064 admits

*2026-11-06 00:33:39*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: ADR-064 — Superseded by ADR-074, which keeps its rule unchanged; cited as the ruling in force when written -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-2175 LIT-2151 LIT-2145 LIT-2179 LIT-2176 LIT-2140 LIT-2173 THEORY-1510 CLAIM-604 CLAIM-600 — Unfetched, Unavailable, Proposed or new; entries this sweep writes or notes -->

The supplied-maintenance filing and its five gap-filling follow-ups (dmarx/nucleation#404 to [#410](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/410)) registered a dozen works as Unavailable that [ADR-053](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-053.md) files as Unfetched, and left unread at least two works that [ADR-064](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-064.md) counts as lawfully readable. The error was the lead's (Claude, in this session), not the readers'. The reader briefs told readers to use only the author's, the publisher's or a repository's own copy. That excluded the course pages, faculty pages and scholarly third-party hosts that [ADR-064](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-064.md) admits. Where a lawful copy was located and the fetch was blocked (a Cloudflare challenge, a WAF challenge, a reset connection, a TLS failure), the briefs had the work filed Unavailable, when [ADR-053](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-053.md) says Unfetched with the address, the blocker and the date.

This sweep corrects the entries on the default branch:

- **Moved to Unfetched**, each with its address, blocker and date in a new status_note and a version-2 history entry: [LIT-2175](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2175.md) (Burning Man's Ten Principles), [LIT-2151](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2151.md) (Rogers & Coates), [LIT-2145](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2145.md) (Holl et al. 2020), [LIT-2179](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2179.md) (Corbin & Holl), [LIT-2176](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2176.md) (Gross et al.) and [LIT-2140](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2140.md) (Ostrom 1996).
  - [LIT-2151](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2151.md) may not qualify. [ADR-053](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-053.md) excludes a copy that is down for everyone, and the USAID host's 503 could mean that. The connection resets point to this client, so it was moved.
  - [LIT-2140](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2140.md)'s São Paulo course copy was located. A reading of it on 2026-11-06 was refused by this session's permission system, not by the host, and was not worked around.
- **Left Unavailable:** [LIT-2173](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2173.md) (Resende et al.). Only the repository's host was recorded, not the item's address, so [ADR-053](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-053.md)'s condition is not met.
- **Read:** Suding, Gross & Houseman 2004 ([LIT-2169](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2169.md)), now Active, from the typeset.io/SciSpace copy, with [NOTE-1700](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1700.md) and [THEORY-1510](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1510.md). Kadowaki et al. ([LIT-2165](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2165.md)) and Schröder et al. ([LIT-2167](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2167.md)), read in its place, now complement it. Dated notes were added to [CLAIM-604](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md) and [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md), and to both stand-ins. Directives that listed [LIT-2169](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2169.md) as Unavailable were pruned.

The same correction went onto the open pull requests, whose entries are not yet on the default branch: Bräutigam & Knack on dmarx/nucleation#406; Wood, Bruner & Ross and Bainbridge on dmarx/nucleation#407, where Cohen & Levinthal 1990 is now read from a copy [ADR-064](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-064.md) admits; and Zabusky & Kruskal and Satsuma & Yajima on dmarx/nucleation#410.

The curation entries and changelog fragments that called these works Unavailable were true of the filing at the time, and they are left as written. This entry is the correction. The Unfetched entries are the owner's queue: a browser fetch of each recorded address is the cheapest way to read them. The fix for the hazard upstream is in the brief, not the net. A reader brief must name [ADR-064](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-064.md)'s admitted copies and [ADR-053](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-053.md)'s Unfetched status. The lead's reader and filer briefs for this session now say so; whether the read-and-file skill should also say so is the owner's call.
